value.summary: Measure how long messages wait behind a busy turn, flag long holds to the PA, add an --urgent send that lands at the next tool boundary, and start role-request limits at delivery.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Messages to a seat in a long turn wait for that turn to end. Today that cost hours (F25). This plan measures the wait per message, has the PA flag waits over 15 minutes, adds `--urgent` for the few messages a working seat must see now (Copilot through onPostToolUse; OMP/Pi already steer; others downgrade with a reason), and makes s12 limits count from delivery (F73). Owner: delivery (pij-swift-kestrel), after plan 212.

sections.name: goals
value: Measure how long messages wait behind a busy turn, flag long holds to the PA, add an --urgent send that lands at the next tool boundary, and start role-request limits at delivery.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Changing FYI semantics or the cold-wake rule.
F68 (--in-reply-to counts as an answer): plan 212.
Any new delivery timer or poll.

value.claim: Measure held time. Every delivery records when it was queued and when its body reached the recipient's session (the Copilot extension's claim, an OMP/Pi steer or prompt, a PTY type, a Claude socket ack), in ms. Check first whether `jobs.enqueued_at` and `jobs.acked_at` already mean exactly that for every rung; if they do, use them and say so in the PR; if not, add the missing column in one migration (claim its number with `pij claim migration`). A message still queued has a live held age.

PA flags long holds. The PA digest lists every message held more than 15 minutes behind a busy turn: recipient, sender, msg id, held minutes, and whether it is still queued. Each message is flagged once, not on every digest. The threshold is a named constant in the store module.

Urgent sends. `pij send <seat|role:...> --urgent` (and `urgent: true` on the native pij_send tool) asks for delivery at the recipient's next tool boundary instead of its turn end. Copilot: the pij extension returns pending urgent bodies as `additionalContext` from `onPostToolUse` and `onPostToolUseFailure`; the message is delivered once and never again at turn end. OMP and Pi already steer mid-turn, so urgent is accepted and changes nothing. Claude: use the socket path if it can reach a running turn, else downgrade. An idle recipient gets an urgent send exactly as a normal one, cold-wake rules included.

Refuse or downgrade with a reason. Where a harness has no tool-boundary hook (Codex, PTY-only seats, a Copilot seat without the native extension), the send goes through as a normal one and the receipt carries a warning naming the harness and why. `--urgent` with `--fyi` is refused (E-RS-URGENT-FYI). Every urgent send writes one spine event (sender, recipient, msg id, outcome: injected, steered or downgraded) so the PA can count them per sender.

F73: limits count from delivery. A role request's `--limit` clock starts when the request reaches the holder's session, not when it was created; until then the request has no check-in. If a check-in fires, it says how long the request was held in delivery. (A reply with --in-reply-to counting as an answer is F68, plan 212; don't duplicate it here.)

Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). No new timer, poll or launch. The held-time record is one column on a write the delivery already makes. The PA flag is one indexed query inside the existing PA digest round, constant per digest, not per seat per tick. The Copilot hook reads an in-memory list the extension's existing stream fills; it makes no daemon call on a tool boundary unless an urgent body is pending. State the per-tool-call cost (expected: a map lookup) and measure the live fleet before and after.

Docs and states. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md: --urgent, the downgrade warning, E-RS-URGENT-FYI, the held-time fields and the limit clock. The pij skill and the pij_send tool description say when to use urgent (the recipient is mid-turn and its current work is wrong without this message) and when not to (everything else; prefer normal or fyi). docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: F25 measured (pm-001, live store, 6 Nov 2026, jobs.enqueued_at to jobs.acked_at for kind delivery:*): 152 of 1,364 deliveries were held over 15 min. pij-local-warbler: 39 of 52 over 15 min, 25 over an hour, max 7.5 h; pij-back-tapir 31 of 48 (max 4 h); pij-swift-kestrel 29 of 38 (max 4 h); pij-wary-lynx 20 of 47 (max 3 h). pm-001's 13:38 to 18:44 sends to warbler reached it between 22:36 and 23:18. That is why #130 needed three asks, and it caused both performance reworks and kestrel's slip. Seams: the daemon queues to Copilot seats with reason extension-stream (crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs, enqueue_carrier); the Copilot extension (.copilot/extensions/pij/extension.mjs) only has onUserPromptSubmitted today, which carries held FYIs. The Copilot SDK (copilot-sdk/types.d.ts) has onPostToolUse and onPostToolUseFailure, whose `additionalContext` the host appends as guidance to the model. OMP/Pi already deliver with deliverAs: steer (.omp/extensions/pij/adapters/pi-runtime.ts). Claude delivery is crates/transport/src/uds.rs. F73 (warbler, 23:19): request 01a1b0ab had a 20 min limit, reached warbler at 23:18:55, was answered at 23:18:59 with --in-reply-to, and the check-in still fired at 23:19:16 because the clock ran from creation.

value.question: Does jobs.acked_at mark the body reaching the session for every rung, or only the daemon handing it to a stream? The answer decides whether AC1 needs a migration.
Should urgent sends be rate-capped per sender? Proposed: no cap at first; the spine event and the PA's per-sender count make abuse visible.
Can the Claude socket path reach a running turn, or is Claude a downgrade for now?

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
